rationale: Both candidates independently surface the core reviewer-validated concern (the `!="cpu"` widening silently enabling untested NPU/XPU RNG paths, which yeahdongcn's inline reply confirms was only meant to cover CUDA+MUSA) and both flag the FL2VA/Ref2VA mislabeled block and the phantom test file — solid overlapping recall on the substantive thread. Neither explicitly proposes the `current_omni_platform.device` abstraction or the UT-reduction/drop-test-file exchange, capping recall similarly for both. X pulls ahead on precision and actionability: it identifies a well-grounded, high-value bug Y entirely misses (torch.random.fork_rng defaults device_type="cuda" and never gets overridden, so the save/restore silently targets the wrong RNG backend on MUSA), backs claims with concrete file:line evidence and drop-in code fixes, while Y's extra findings (torch-version-floor ask, TID251 style nit) are thinner and less load-bearing.
